chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, and Muhammad ibn Ali, together from Ismail ibn Mihran, and Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Ali ibn al-Hasan al-Taymi, and Ali ibn al-Husayn, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, together from Ismail ibn Mihran, from al-Munzir ibn Jayfar, from al-Hakam ibn Zuhayr, from Abdullah ibn Jarir al-Abdi, from al-Asbagh ibn Nubata, who said:

Abdullah ibn Umar, and the son of Abu Bakr, and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas came to the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him), seeking preferential treatment for themselves. So he ascended the pulpit, and the people turned towards him.

So he said: All praise is to Allah, the Patron of Praise, and the utmost limit of Generosity. Descriptions do not encompass Him, nor is He defined by languages, nor is He known by limits. And I testify that there is no god except Allah, One, with no partner, and that Muhammad (peace be upon him and his family) is the Messenger of Allah, the Prophet of Guidance, and the place of Piety, and the Messenger of the Highest Lord. He came with the Truth from the Presence of the Truth, to warn by the Illuminating Quran and the Illuminating Proof. So he declared by the Manifest Book and proceeded upon what the former Messengers had proceeded upon.

Now then, O people! Do not let men say that the world had overwhelmed them, so they acquired property, made canals flow, rode the finest beasts, and wore the softest clothes. That would become a source of shame and ignominy for them if the Forgiver does not forgive them. If I were to prevent them from what they were indulging in and turn them to what they deserve, they would lose that and ask, saying: 'The son of Abu Talib has been unjust to us, deprived us, and prevented us from our rights.'

So Allah is the Helper against those who face our Qiblah, eat our slaughtered animals, believe in our Prophet, testify our testimony, and enter our religion. We will apply upon them the judgment of the Quran and the limits of Islam. There is no preference for anyone over anyone else except by piety. Indeed, for the pious, with Allah the Exalted, is the best reward, the best recompense, and the best return. Allah, Blessed and Exalted, did not make the world the reward for the pious, and what is with Allah is better for the righteous.

Look, O people of the religion of Allah, at what you found in the Book of Allah and what you left with the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and strove for in the cause of Allah. Is it by lineage, or by ancestry, or by deed, or by obedience, or by asceticism? And regarding what you were desirous of, hasten to your dwellings. May Allah have mercy on you. They are the inhabited ones, which do not decay, the lasting ones, which do not perish, to which He invited you, encouraged you, and made you eager, and made the reward for them with Him.

So complete the bounties of Allah, Exalted is His mention, by submission to His decree and gratitude for His favors. Whoever is not pleased with this is not from us, nor is he to us. Indeed, the ruler judges by the judgment of Allah, and there is no fear upon him for that. Those are the successful ones. And in one copy: 'And no loneliness,' and those are they upon whom there is no fear, nor shall they grieve.

And he said: 'And I have admonished you with my whip, with which I admonish my family, but you did not care. And I struck you with my whip, by which I establish the limits of my Lord, but you did not cease. Do you want that I should strike you with my sword? Indeed, I know what you want, and how to straighten your unevenness. But I will not buy your correction for the spoiling of myself. Rather, Allah will make a people overcome you and exact revenge for me from you. So you will have no world that you enjoyed, and no Hereafter that you turned to. Thus, remote and crushed are the companions of the Blaze.'
ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say about preferential treatment and piety in his sermon to the companions?
ai.summary: This sermon, delivered by Imam Ali (peace be upon him) to prominent companions like Abdullah ibn Umar and Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, addresses the political and social tensions regarding preferential treatment based on lineage or wealth. The Imam clarifies that true superiority in Islam is rooted in piety (taqwa) rather than status, warning that strict enforcement of their rights would lead to complaints of injustice, thereby preserving unity. He concludes by asserting that divine judgment is based on God's decree and that true success lies in the Hereafter, emphasizing the importance of submitting to God's will.
